<figure id="S4.F6" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2512.13655v2/fig5_coverage_matrix.png" id="S4.F6.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:648/518;" width="648" height="518" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 6: </span>Tool compatibility matrix across sixteen models. Heretic achieved universal compatibility (16/16 models), followed by DECCP (11/16). FailSpy’s TransformerLens dependency limited compatibility to 5 models, while ErisForge succeeded on 9 models with some failures on models using non-standard architectures. Gray indicates not tested; Mamba SSM models are architecturally incompatible with transformer-only tools (see Table <a href="#S4.T5" title="Table 5 ‣ 4.4 Model Coverage ‣ 4 Results" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>).</figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S4.SS4.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS4.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.SS4.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Coverage Totals</span>: Heretic: 16/16 (100%), DECCP: 11/16 (69%), FailSpy: 5/16 (31%), ErisForge: 9/16 (56%).</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S5" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">5 </span>Discussion</h2>

<section id="S5.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">5.1 </span>Tool Selection Considerations</h3>

<div id="S5.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Based on this evaluation, the following patterns emerged across different use contexts:</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.SS1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Quality-compliance optimization</span>: Heretic’s Bayesian optimization produced the lowest observed KL divergence (minimum 0.043; range 0.043–1.646) but required the longest processing time (<math id="S5.SS1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sim" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>∼</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sim</annotation></semantics></math>45 min).</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.SS1.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Capability preservation priority</span>: ErisForge and DECCP showed the lowest benchmark degradation (avg GSM8K <math id="S5.SS1.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta</annotation></semantics></math>: <math id="S5.SS1.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-0.28" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>0.28</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-0.28</annotation></semantics></math> pp and <math id="S5.SS1.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-0.13" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>0.13</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-0.13</annotation></semantics></math> pp respectively).</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS1.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS1.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.SS1.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Mamba/hybrid architectures</span>: Only Heretic successfully processed SSM-containing models (falcon-mamba-7b-instruct).</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS1.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS1.p5.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.SS1.p5.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Processing efficiency</span>: DECCP completed in <math id="S5.SS1.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sim" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>∼</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sim</annotation></semantics></math>2 min vs Heretic’s <math id="S5.SS1.p5.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sim" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>∼</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sim</annotation></semantics></math>45 min (20<math id="S5.SS1.p5.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>×</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\times</annotation></semantics></math> faster).</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">5.2 </span>Hypothesis Evaluation</h3>

<div id="S5.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.SS2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">H1 (Model Dependence)</span> is supported by substantial variance in both KL divergence and residual refusals across models (Table <a href="#S4.T2" title="Table 2 ‣ 4.1 Heretic Abliteration Results ‣ 4 Results" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>). Across these eight Heretic-evaluated models, KL divergence and remaining refusals are strongly correlated (Pearson <math id="S5.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r=0.87" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.87</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r=0.87</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S5.SS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p=0.005" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.005</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p=0.005</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S5.SS2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n=8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n=8</annotation></semantics></math>), consistent with a coupled trade-off between distribution shift and refusal suppression (Figure <a href="#S4.F2" title="Figure 2 ‣ 4.1 Heretic Abliteration Results ‣ 4 Results" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>).</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.SS2.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">H2 (Capability Preservation)</span> is supported on the benchmarked subset: single-pass methods (DECCP/ErisForge) show smaller average benchmark changes than Heretic (Table <a href="#S4.T4" title="Table 4 ‣ 4.3 Tool Comparison Summary ‣ 4 Results" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>), and the largest divergence appears on GSM8K (Table <a href="#S4.T3" title="Table 3 ‣ 4.2 Benchmark Preservation Results ‣ 4 Results" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>).</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS2.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.SS2.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">H3 (Alignment Sensitivity, Case Study)</span> is consistent with the DPO-only Zephyr-7B-beta exhibiting the lowest residual refusals and highest ASR under Heretic (Table <a href="#S4.T2" title="Table 2 ‣ 4.1 Heretic Abliteration Results ‣ 4 Results" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>). However, stronger conclusions require additional DPO-only models and consistent baseline coverage.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">5.3 </span>Limitations</h3>

<div id="S5.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Several limitations should inform interpretation of these findings:</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS3.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.SS3.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Statistical Rigor</span>: Due to computational constraints, the primary results reflect single experimental runs rather than multiple independent trials with variance estimation. While Heretic’s Bayesian optimization internally evaluates multiple configurations (50 trials), each final abliterated model represents a single optimization outcome. This design choice was driven by practical considerations: full benchmark evaluation of a single 7B model requires approximately 4 to 6 GPU-hours, making triplicate runs across 16 models and 4 tools prohibitively expensive (<math id="S5.SS3.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="&gt;" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>&gt;</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">&gt;</annotation></semantics></math>1,500 GPU-hours). To mitigate this limitation, deterministic execution was ensured (fixed seeds, deterministic CUDA where possible) and complete reproducibility artifacts are provided enabling independent replication. Future work with dedicated compute resources should incorporate proper bootstrap confidence intervals and statistical significance testing across multiple runs. Notably, the observed effect sizes for tool comparisons (e.g., Yi-1.5-9B GSM8K: Heretic 52.08% vs DECCP 72.40%, <math id="S5.SS3.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta=20.32" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>20.32</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta=20.32</annotation></semantics></math> pp) substantially exceed benchmark uncertainty (GSM8K 95% CI half-width <math id="S5.SS3.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sim" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>∼</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sim</annotation></semantics></math>2.4–2.7 pp; Appendix), suggesting robust underlying differences despite single-run methodology.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS3.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS3.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.SS3.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Metric Coverage</span>: The capability evaluation focuses on three benchmarks (MMLU, GSM8K, HellaSwag). Due to tool compatibility constraints and computational budget, baseline-relative cross-tool comparisons were limited to three models (DeepSeek-7B, Mistral-7B, Yi-1.5-9B); Zephyr-7B-beta is included without a base-model baseline. While compatibility was assessed across 16 models, quantitative metrics (KL divergence, refusals, and benchmark deltas) are not available for every model-tool pair. Additionally, these benchmarks may not capture all forms of capability degradation (e.g., instruction-following quality, long-context coherence, or domain-specific expertise).</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS3.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS3.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.SS3.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Refusal/ASR Validity</span>: Refusal rate and ASR rely on a marker-based detection heuristic and may misclassify outputs. False positives can occur when responses mention safety language (e.g., “illegal”) while still providing actionable content; false negatives can occur when refusals are phrased without the selected markers. Additionally, refusal rates are estimated from <math id="S5.SS3.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n=100" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>100</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n=100</annotation></semantics></math> prompts per model and therefore have non-trivial sampling uncertainty (Appendix). As a lightweight validity check, we cross-validated the marker heuristic using an independent RoBERTa-based refusal/disclaimer classifier trained on Chatbot Arena responses <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib6" title="" class="ltx_ref">6</a>]</cite>. Disagreements were dominated by disclaimer-style outputs, suggesting that marker-based ASR can be conservative (i.e., under-estimate refusal bypass) when models retain safety language while still answering (Appendix Table <a href="#Sx4.T8" title="Table 8 ‣ C. Automated Refusal Heuristic Cross-Validation ‣ Appendix: Additional Uncertainty and Validity Checks" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a>). As a result, ASR should be interpreted as a proxy for refusal suppression rather than a definitive measure of harmful content generation.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS3.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS3.p5.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.SS3.p5.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Tool Configuration and Budget</span>: Tools were evaluated using their recommended default settings. This can conflate algorithmic differences with configuration choices and compute budgets (e.g., multi-trial optimization vs single-pass ablation). Future work should compare tools under matched compute budgets or matched refusal-rate targets (Pareto curves of refusal suppression, KL divergence, and capability).</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS3.p6" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS3.p6.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.SS3.p6.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Model Selection</span>: The sixteen-model evaluation, while architecturally diverse, represents a subset of available instruction-tuned models. Notably absent are larger models (<math id="S5.SS3.p6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="&gt;" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>&gt;</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">&gt;</annotation></semantics></math>14B parameters), mixture-of-experts architectures (e.g., Mixtral), and models from some providers (Claude, GPT). Results may not generalize to these architectures, particularly for models employing novel safety training techniques or different internal representational structures.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS3.p7" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS3.p7.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.SS3.p7.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Long-term and Deployment Effects</span>: This study evaluates immediate post-abliteration performance under controlled benchmark conditions. Real-world deployment introduces variables not captured here: multi-turn conversation drift, distribution shift from user prompts differing from evaluation sets, and potential emergent behaviors under extended use. Whether abliterated models maintain stability over thousands of interactions remains uncharacterized.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S6" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">6 </span>Conclusion</h2>

<div id="S6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">This study presented a systematic comparison of four LLM abliteration tools (Heretic, DECCP, ErisForge, and FailSpy/abliterator) across sixteen instruction-tuned models, reporting tool compatibility across all models and capability preservation benchmarks on a subset due to tool and compute constraints. The evaluation yielded the following findings:</p>
</div>
<div id="S6.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S6.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">1. Capability preservation varied significantly by tool.</span> In the benchmarked subset, ErisForge exhibited the lowest average benchmark degradation (MMLU: <math id="S6.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-0.12" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>0.12</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-0.12</annotation></semantics></math> pp, GSM8K: <math id="S6.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-0.28" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>0.28</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-0.28</annotation></semantics></math> pp, HellaSwag: <math id="S6.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-0.08" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>0.08</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-0.08</annotation></semantics></math> pp), followed by DECCP (GSM8K: <math id="S6.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-0.13" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>0.13</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-0.13</annotation></semantics></math> pp). Heretic demonstrated model-specific variance, with minimal impact on Mistral-7B (<math id="S6.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-0.12" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>0.12</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-0.12</annotation></semantics></math> pp avg) but substantial GSM8K degradation on Yi-1.5-9B (<math id="S6.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-18.81" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>18.81</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-18.81</annotation></semantics></math> pp; <math id="S6.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-26.5\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mn>26.5</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-26.5\%</annotation></semantics></math> relative).</p>
</div>
<div id="S6.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S6.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">2. Mathematical reasoning showed highest sensitivity to abliteration.</span> GSM8K scores exhibited the largest variance across tools and models (range: <math id="S6.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+1.51" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>1.51</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+1.51</annotation></semantics></math> pp to <math id="S6.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-18.81" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>18.81</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-18.81</annotation></semantics></math> pp), suggesting potential overlap between mathematical reasoning circuits and refusal-related representations.</p>
</div>
<div id="S6.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S6.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">3. Automated optimization produced quality-speed tradeoffs.</span> Heretic’s Bayesian optimization achieved a minimum KL divergence of 0.043 (range: 0.043–1.646) with explicit refusal tracking, but required <math id="S6.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sim" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>∼</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sim</annotation></semantics></math>45 minutes per model. DECCP and ErisForge completed processing in <math id="S6.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sim" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>∼</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sim</annotation></semantics></math>2–20 minutes with more predictable capability preservation.</p>
</div>
<div id="S6.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.p5.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S6.p5.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">4. Model compatibility differed substantially across tools.</span> Heretic processed all 16 tested models (100% coverage), while DECCP supported 11/16 (69%), ErisForge 9/16 (56%), and FailSpy 5/16 (31%).</p>
</div>
<div id="S6.p6" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.p6.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S6.p6.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">5. Model resilience varied across architectures.</span> Mistral-7B exhibited consistent stability across all tools (avg <math id="S6.p6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta</annotation></semantics></math>: <math id="S6.p6.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-0.12" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>0.12</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-0.12</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="S6.p6.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-0.61" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>0.61</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-0.61</annotation></semantics></math> pp), while Yi-1.5-9B showed high sensitivity to Heretic’s kernel-weighted approach but improved GSM8K performance (<math id="S6.p6.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+1.51" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>1.51</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+1.51</annotation></semantics></math> pp) with DECCP.</p>
</div>
<div id="S6.p7" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.p7.1" class="ltx_p">These findings establish empirical baselines for tool comparison and provide reproducible protocols for evaluating abliteration approaches.</p>
</div>
<div id="S6.p8" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.p8.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S6.p8.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Future Directions.</span> Several promising extensions merit investigation. Recent contributions to the llm-abliteration repository <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib5" title="" class="ltx_ref">5</a>]</cite> have extended support to Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architectures, enabling abliteration of models such as Mixtral and DeepSeek-MoE that were previously incompatible with transformer-focused tools. Additionally, the introduction of an “invert” option enables directional <em id="S6.p8.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">addition</em> rather than removal, potentially amplifying specific behavioral traits—a capability that opens novel applications in steering model personality, enhancing helpfulness, or studying the symmetric effects of representation engineering. Systematic evaluation of these extensions across MoE architectures and bidirectional modification scenarios represents a natural continuation of this work.</p>
</div>
</section>

<section id="Sx4.SSx3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection">C. Automated Refusal Heuristic Cross-Validation</h3>

<div id="Sx4.SSx3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Sx4.SSx3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To bound refusal/ASR heuristic misclassification without human labeling, we compared the marker-based refusal heuristic used in this paper against an independent RoBERTa-based refusal/disclaimer classifier <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib6" title="" class="ltx_ref">6</a>]</cite> on existing generations from a separate harmful-prompt set (150 prompts per model, six abliterated models; <math id="Sx4.SSx3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n=900" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>900</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n=900</annotation></semantics></math> responses). The classifier distinguishes refusals from disclaimers; for this comparison, disclaimers are treated as non-refusals (i.e., counted toward ASR) because they attempt to answer while citing constraints. Table <a href="#Sx4.T8" title="Table 8 ‣ C. Automated Refusal Heuristic Cross-Validation ‣ Appendix: Additional Uncertainty and Validity Checks" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a> reports agreement metrics for the full marker set (paper default) and a stricter variant that drops generic safety-topic substrings (e.g., “illegal”, “unethical”) to illustrate sensitivity.</p>
</div>
<figure id="Sx4.T8" class="ltx_table">

<span id="Sx4.T9.2.8.1.1.1" class="ltx_p"><math id="Sx4.T9.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta=\text{ASR}_{\text{classifier}}-\text{ASR}_{\text{markers}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathsize="0.800em" mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo mathsize="0.800em">=</mo><mrow><msub><mtext mathsize="0.800em">ASR</mtext><mtext mathsize="0.800em">classifier</mtext></msub><mo mathsize="0.800em">−</mo><msub><mtext mathsize="0.800em">ASR</mtext><mtext mathsize="0.800em">markers</mtext></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta=\text{ASR}_{\text{classifier}}-\text{ASR}_{\text{markers}}</annotation></semantics></math><span id="Sx4.T9.2.8.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">; positive values indicate the marker heuristic is more conservative (flags more outputs as refusals). “Disclaimers” are classifier labels indicating safety/capability caveats while still attempting to answer (counted as non-refusal for ASR in this table).</span></span>
</span></th></tr>
